𝐌𝐌𝐃𝐀 𝐒𝐓𝐀𝐑𝐓𝐒 𝐖𝐎𝐑𝐊 𝐎𝐍 𝐀𝐍 𝐈𝐓𝐒 𝐏𝐋𝐀𝐍 𝐅𝐎𝐑 𝐌𝐄𝐓𝐑𝐎 𝐌𝐀𝐍𝐈𝐋𝐀 𝐓𝐎 𝐈𝐌𝐏𝐑𝐎𝐕𝐄 𝐓𝐑𝐀𝐅𝐅𝐈𝐂 𝐀𝐍𝐃 𝐒𝐀𝐅𝐄𝐓𝐘

Representatives from various agencies and personnel from the Metropolitan Manila Development Authority, as well as the academia, underwent a recent planning workshop spearheaded by the Metro Manila Intelligent Transportation Systems (MMITS) Project’s technical working groups and the expert team from Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) to craft an ITS development plan for Metro Manila to ease congestion and improve safety.

The workshop identified current issues, future challenges, objectives, and ITS user services from various aspects, such as traffic signal control, road and incident management, public transportation, freight and logistics, safety and accident prevention, and disaster and emergency management, in order to develop an ITS development plan.

Traffic Engineering Center (TEC) director and MMITS project manager Engr. Francisco Pesino Jr. welcomed the participants and said that the workshop is an opportunity “to deepen understanding, exchange knowledge, and improve collaboration among related  government agencies as  we provide a safer, smarter, and more efficient transportation system for all.”

Mr. Takeshi Matsunuma, project team leader, presented the MMITS’s overall objectives and
deliverables, highlighting the vital role TWG members play in this JICA project in terms of strategic planning, implementation, and performance monitoring.

The project’s ITS development expert Tetsuya Sato, meanwhile, explained the various ITS user services as part of the preparation of an ITS development plan that is scalable, adaptive, and tailored to Metro Manila’s traffic conditions.

Physical Planning and Spatial Development Service director and project coordinator Michael Gison  said that the workshop was a welcome development as new insights on ITS technologies were shared during the activity. He described AI as the current buzzword, which can be used in a fruitful way to optimize traffic management and safety.

He likewise underscored the collaboration with the Department of Science and Technology (DOST) and  other national government agencies in achieving an ITS for Metro Manila.

The ITS development plan is envisioned to support the MMDA’s vision, through the leadership of Chairman Atty. Don Artes, of developing efficient, commuter-oriented, and smart transportation systems in Metro Manila to complement the recently formulated comprehensive traffic management plan.

The ITS development planning workshop was attended by representatives from government agencies including the DOST, Department of Transportation (DOTr), Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH), Department of Economy, Planning, and Development (DEPDEV), LTFRB, Land Transportation Office, and the National Center for Transportation Studies.

#mmda #mmits

‘’YUN AY FREEDOM OF SPEECH AND EXPRESSION’

Ipinagtataka umano ni Vice Pres. Sara Duterte kung bakit itinuturing ng kasalukuyang administrasyon na destabilisasyon ang panawagan ng ilang mga grupo na magbitiw na si Pres. Bongbong Marcos sa kanyang puwesto sa gitna ng malawakang korupsyon sa flood control projects.

“Kahit man mag-rally ang mga tao araw-araw sa EDSA, hindi destabilisasyon ‘yan… Pagpapahayag ‘yan ng galit mo, paghahanap ‘yan ng accountability [at] transparency sa administrasyon,” giit ng bise sa Pandesal Forum ngayong Huwebes, Oct. 16.

“Duda ko, natatakot sila sa posibleng mangyari sa kanila... Alam ko na insecure... Makikita mo, medyo paranoid,” dagdag niya.
